The instant Criminal Appeal is preferred under Section 14(A)(2) of the Scheduled Caste and Scheduled Tribe (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989 (in short "the Atrocities Act") against the Order dated 16.04.2024, passed by the Learned Special Judge (Atrocities Act) Jashpur, Chhattisgarh, in Special Sessions Case No. 23 of 2023, whereby the bail application under Section 439 of CRPC, filed by the appellant in connection with Crime No. 125 of 2023, registered at Police Outpost, Pandrapath Police Station, Bagicha District, Jashpur for the offences punishable under Sections 366, 376,
376(D), 294, 506(B), 323, 34 of IPC and Section 3(2)(v) of Scheduled Caste and Neutral Citation Scheduled Tribe (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989, has been rejected.
2.

sentences.text: The facts of the case in brief are that the prosecutrix has made a written complaint to the Police Station on 04.09.2023, that the appellant and other co-accused person have forcefully taken her towards Danagari Waterfall and before reaching to Danagari Waterfall, near Darwakona Jungle and Satinala, in an isolated place, they stopped the motorcycle and tried to take the prosecutrix inside the jungle, when she tried to raise her alarm, the present Appellant slapped her twice and threaten to kill her.
The accused persons took her away from the road and committed rape upon her one by one.
On the report made by the prosecutrix, FIR has been registered.

She was medically examined Saddam Khan vs State Of Chhattisgarh on 10 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/55534783/
1 and the statement of witnesses have been recorded, in which the present Appellant has been arrested on 10.09.2023.

sentences.text: 3. Learned counsel for the Appellant would submit that the Appellant is innocent and has been falsely implicated in the offence with intention to extort money from the present Appellant, a false report has been lodged by the prosecutrix.
She on her own will, went to visit Danagari Waterfall along with the Appellant and when her relatives saw her along with the present Appellant, she lodged a report to save herself

, Learned counsel for the Appellant would further submit that the prosecutrix has been examined before the learned Trial Court as PW-1 and has specifically stated that the present Appellant has done nothing with her.

He would also submit that there is no allegation that the prosecutrix was subjected to rape on the ground that she belongs Neutral Citation to Scheduled Caste or Scheduled Tribe community and therefore, the offence under the Atrocities Act is prima facie not made out.
He would also submit that the present Appellant is in jail since 10.09.2023, the final adjudication of the case will take its own time.
Therefore, the Appellant may be released on bail.

4. Per contra, learned counsel for the State, while opposing the submissions made by the learned counsel for the Appellant, would submit that the prosecutrix was forcefully taken by the present Appellant and other co-accused towards Danagari Waterfall and on the way both of them have committed rape upon her one by one.
Injuries have been found on her private part on her medical examination done on 04.09.2023.
The report has been lodged immediately.
As per the FSL report available in the case diary, the semen and sperms were found in the vaginal swab of the prosecutrix.

From the 161 CRPC and 164 CRPC statement of the prosecutrix as well as the other witnesses, it is prima facie appears that the prosecutrix was subjected to gang rape by the present Appellant and other co-accused.

He would also submit that although the prosecutrix has been examined as PW-1 before the learned Trial Court, but her evidence cannot be considered and appreciated at this stage,
therefore, the present appeal of the Appellant claiming bail is liable to be dismissed.
5. I have heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the case diary.
6.
Perusal of the case diary would show that the report has been lodged immediately.
Injuries have been found on the body of the prosecutrix.
Neutral Citation
The presence of semen and sperms are reported in FSL report in the vaginal swab of the prosecutrix.
From her 161 and 164 CRPC statement, there are allegations against the present Appellant and other co-accused.

Although the prosecutrix has been examined before the learned Trial Court as PW-1 and the copy of which has been annexed as Annexure A/2 with the present appeal, but the evidence of the prosecutrix requires consideration, which cannot be appreciated at the stage of considering the bail application under Section 439 of CRPC.

From the evidence available in the case diary and charge-sheet, the prima facie material available against the present Appellant to implicate in the alleged offence of gang rape, I am not inclined to release the Appellant on bail.
7. Consequently, the appeal filed by the Appellant is dismissed.
